# Deferral Ledger

One line per deferral. Never close a task silently with a forward reference —
record what landed, what was deferred, and where to resume.

The `status` column tracks consumption of each deferral by milestone **M0119**
(see `docs/milestones/0119-deferral-ledger-backlog-consumption.md`). Values:
`-` = open / 未対応 (not yet consumed); `resolved` = the deferred scope has since
landed (by a later ledger row, a promotion, or current code) and has been
verified by an M0119 triage/consumption task. M0119 sets these values; appending
a new deferral row uses `-`.

This silently changes the predicate's meaning (not just its NULL semantics) whenever the correlation column differs from the IN operand and/or the subquery's SELECT column — demonstrated live: `x IN (SELECT y FROM t2 WHERE z = outer.w)` matched on `w = y` alone, ignoring `z` and the actual `x`/`y` comparison (`ci_outer`/`ci_inner` repro: `x=1,w=5` wrongly matched `y=5,z=777` even though no row has `z=5`). Fixed by gating `canUnnestInExprDepth`'s correlated branch on a new `correlatedInOperandSafeToUnnest` check: `in.Operand` must be the same column as the correlation's outer-scope side AND the subquery's sole projected column must be the same column as the correlation's subquery-scope side. Proved as a corollary that this closes item (1) above for free: when both identities hold, every surviving row's projected value is non-NULL and exactly equals `in.Operand` (the equality correlation can't be satisfied by NULL), so a plain (non-NullAware) Anti join already gives correct NOT IN semantics — no per-correlation-group NullAware tracking is needed for anything this mechanism still unnests post-fix. Sibling-path catch: the parser Form-2 `splitEmbeddedInterval` (`internal/parser/select.go`) greedily split `1-2 days`→(mag `1-2`,unit `day`), short-circuiting ParseIntervalBody with "invalid interval count"; now guarded to require parts[0] be a plain ParseIntervalMagnitude so year-month bodies fall through to the shared decoder — keeps `interval '…'` (evalIntervalLit) and `::interval`/CAST (parseIntervalCastString) in lock-step. Verified end-to-end over the wire against cmd/goopg: all three SETs succeed, SHOW/pg_settings report them, SET='lz4' moves the value, 'zstd' rejected. Tests: internal/config/object_default_guc_stubs_test.go (TestObjectDefaultGUCStubs, TestObjectDefaultGUCValuesAccepted); internal/catalog/catalog_test.go TestPgSettingsObjectDefaultGUCs. Design: docs/design/root-0004-configuration-and-guc.md new "object-creation default GUC stubs" section. | Behavioral no-op: goopg only implements the heap access method, has no real tablespaces, and picks a column's TOAST compression from its own built-in default rather than consulting default_toast_compression — so a non-default SET (e.g. default_tablespace='ts1', default_toast_compression='lz4' as the session default for an unqualified column) is accepted and ignored, whereas real PG honours all three at CREATE TABLE time (default_tablespace via DefineRelation reloptions, default_table_access_method via the table AM lookup, default_toast_compression via BuildDescForRelation's attcompression default). | To honour behaviour: thread the live default_tablespace / default_table_access_method / default_toast_compression session values into internal/executor CREATE TABLE (operators_ddl.go createTableOp) so an unqualified table picks up the session default. Oracle: postgres/src/backend/commands/tablecmds.c DefineRelation (default_tablespace / accessMethod), src/backend/catalog/heap.c (attcompression default from default_toast_compression). | goopg supports only the heap AM and has no tablespace placement, so the table-AM/tablespace halves are inert until those subsystems exist; the compression-default half is a bounded future slice. The registration (which unblocks real-PG dump replay + pg_settings tooling) is the high-value bounded slice. ONE task per loop. |
| - | 2026-07-12 | PGLZ varlena compression (encode+decode PG parity) | New stdlib-only leaf pkg `internal/pglz` (Compress/Decompress/BuildCompressedVarlena/DecodeInlineCompressed) is a faithful port of PG's `pg_lzcompress.c` + `varatt.h`. Fixed three PG-incompatibilities in the old bootstrap compressor (`internal/initdb/pglz.go`): (1) inverted control-bit polarity (goopg bit1=literal; PG bit1=match), (2) swapped match-tag nibble layout (goopg len in high nibble; PG len in low nibble, `off=((b0&0xf0)<<4)\|b1`) + missing length extension byte for matches 18..273, (3) `va_tcinfo` written `rawSize<<2\|method` instead of PG18's low-30-bits rawsize / top-2-bits method (VARLENA_EXTSIZE_BITS=30). Added the previously-absent decompressor and wired it into BOTH varlena decode twins — `executor.decodePhysicalPGVarlena` (codec.go) and `wal.pgoDecodePhysicalVarlena` (pgoutput.go) — which used to hard-error "compressed varlena not supported". A real PG standby can now decompress goopg's bootstrap `pg_rewrite.ev_action`, and goopg can decode PG-produced inline-compressed varlenas. Tests: internal/pglz/pglz_test.go (round-trip + hand-authored PG-spec token stream independent of our encoder + corrupt-stream + framing/bit-layout + LZ4-reject); executor/codec_compressed_test.go; wal/pgoutput_compressed_test.go; updated tcinfo assertions in initdb pg_rewrite_bootstrap_test.go + btree_search_test.go. Design: docs/design/0046-0007-pglz-varlena-compression.md. LZ4 (ToastCompressionId 1) is rejected not implemented. (3) **`guc`** — `SHOW datestyle` default mismatch (`ISO, MDY` vs PG's `Postgres, MDy` — see finding below) plus goopg's `DateStyle` GUC assignment doesn't implement PG's two-token partial-set semantics (`SET datestyle = 'SQL'` should preserve the existing MDY/DMY/YMD order component and only replace the style word; goopg's `SHOW datestyle` output shows only the style, dropping the order entirely) nor the `SQL`/`German`/`Postgres` non-ISO OUTPUT FORMATS for timestamp/date rendering (goopg only emits ISO-style). User chose **FULL PG-IDENTICAL: WAL_LOG transport + OID preservation** (via AskUserQuestion) over the lower-fidelity options. Why the design fork existed: goopg's CREATE DATABASE DEVIATES from PG — it copies template0's catalog image (base/4) + re-registers the named template's USER tables under FRESH OIDs (copyTemplateTables, catalog.AllocOID) via a RAW non-WAL-logged byte copy (copyRelationFileFsync), whereas PG copies the named template's whole dir PRESERVING relOids and (PG15+ default) WAL-logs every block (XLOG_DBASE_CREATE_WAL_LOG + per-block FPI). So there's no clean map to PG's RM_DBASE records without changing goopg semantics. PG record formats (postgres/src/include/commands/dbcommands_xlog.h): XLOG_DBASE_CREATE_FILE_COPY=0x00 {db_id,ts_id,src_db_id,src_ts_id}; XLOG_DBASE_CREATE_WAL_LOG=0x10 {db_id,ts_id}; XLOG_DBASE_DROP=0x20 {db_id,ntablespaces,ts_ids[]}. The 37th row's open design question — how to thread the time-of-day fields through the `time.Date` construction — is answered by NOT hand-parsing them: the fallback substitutes a leap PROXY YEAR (`bcLeapProxyYear = 2000`) into the date token and re-parses the candidate through the ordinary `pgTimestampLayouts` table, so time of day, fractional seconds, the `T` separator and every zone spelling are decoded by the same code as all other input (a private time-of-day parser here would be a fourth instance of the two-table drift that table exists to end), then rebuilds the decoded wall clock at the real astronomical year via `time.Date` — which performs `ApplyEra`'s literal->astronomical shift by hand, as the DATE fallback does. The zone rule is applied to the PROXY value before the rebuild and the resulting whole-day movement is measured and re-applied with `AddDate`, because `tsApplyZone` can cross midnight (`'0001-02-29 00:30:00+05:30 BC'::timestamptz` is the 28th in UTC). Hooking INSIDE the candidate loop (not after it) is what lets the hour-24/leap-second canonicalized candidate still take its turn, so `'0001-02-29 24:00:00 BC'` composes to March 1st with `carry=1`. PG 18.3 oracle captured live for six inputs (both zone modes, the day carry, astronomical -4, and the impossible `0001-02-30`); all agree. Gates: `TestBCLeapDayTimestampDecodesAtTheAstronomicalYear` (asserts the DECODED FIELDS, since the carrier refuses every BC value regardless and a SQLSTATE-only assertion would pass with the fields wrong) and `TestBCLeapDayTimestampFallbackKeepsTheErrorClasses`, both mutation-checked by short-circuiting the fallback. | Nothing of the BC leap-day race itself. A BC timestamp still cannot be STORED — the nanosecond `KindTime` carrier (1677..2262) refuses it — but that is the standing 282-reference carrier row, not this one. | — | — |
